globalSettings.s_identity.title: Identity
globalSettings.s_identity.description: How this host identifies itself on the tailnet. Click "Connect to Tailscale" on the Mesh page to start the browser-redirect login flow.
globalSettings.s_identity.clientMode.des: Host = drive the system-installed Tailscale (requires it installed + running on the machine). Onboard = the addon downloads its own Tailscale build and runs a dedicated tailscaled in userspace mode — no system install needed, isolated mesh identity for the hub. Changing this restarts the addon.
globalSettings.s_identity.hostname.label: Device Hostname
globalSettings.s_identity.hostname.descr: Override the hostname advertised in the tailnet. Empty = use the OS hostname.
globalSettings.s_routes.title: Subnet routing
globalSettings.s_routes.description: Control which subnet routes flow between this host and the rest of the tailnet (`tailscale set --accept-routes` / `--advertise-routes`).
globalSettings.s_routes.acceptRoutes.des: Install subnet routes other peers advertise (e.g. a peer router exposing `192.168.60.0/24`).
globalSettings.s_routes.advertisedRoutes: Comma-separated CIDRs this host exposes to peers (e.g. `192.168.10.0/24,10.0.0.0/8`). Requires approval in the Tailscale admin console.
globalSettings.s_routes.advertisedTags.d: Comma-separated tags this host declares (e.g. `tag:server,tag:camera-host`). Must be allowed by the tailnet policy.
globalSettings.s_dns-exit.title: DNS & exit node
globalSettings.s_dns-exit.description: How this host resolves names + whether all egress traffic routes through a peer.
globalSettings.s_dns-exit.acceptDns.desc: Use DNS resolvers the tailnet provides (MagicDNS + split-DNS). Disabling keeps the OS resolver.
globalSettings.s_dns-exit.exitNodeId.des: Route all internet egress through this peer. Empty to disable. Use the peer ID from the Peers tab.
globalSettings.s_access.title: Access
globalSettings.s_access.description: Server-side access controls applied by the daemon.
globalSettings.s_access.shieldsUp.label: Shields up
globalSettings.s_access.shieldsUp.descri: Block ALL incoming connections from peers. Outgoing connections still work.
globalSettings.s_access.ssh.label: Enable Tailscale SSH
globalSettings.s_access.ssh.description: Run the daemon's SSH server on this host. Lets peers SSH in via MagicDNS without managing keys.
globalSettings.s_auth-advanced.title: Headless / Auth key
globalSettings.s_auth-advanced.descripti: Use a pre-generated auth key from admin.tailscale.com → Settings → Keys for headless / CI flows where opening a browser is not possible. When set, the addon also auto-rejoins on boot if the daemon dropped offline (5/15/30/60/60 min backoff).
globalSettings.s_auth-advanced.authKey.d: tskey-auth-* token from the Tailscale admin console. Leave empty when using the browser-redirect flow.
globalSettings.s_tailscale-ingress.title: Tailscale Ingress
globalSettings.s_tailscale-ingress.descr: ⚠️ Requires the Tailscale Client addon installed AND the host joined to a tailnet — open System → Mesh Networks → Connect first. Expose the hub via Tailscale Serve (in-tailnet HTTPS) or Funnel (publicly reachable on the internet).
Serve = in-tailnet only (requires the visitor to be on the same tailnet). Funnel = publicly reachable on the internet.
globalSettings.s_tailscale-ingress.sourc: Local port to expose. Use 4443 to forward the hub HTTPS backend.
globalSettings.s_tailscale-ingress.targe: Public-side mount path. Leave empty for root.
globalSettings.s_tailscale-ingress.upstr: How Tailscale reaches the local hub. The hub listens HTTPS with a self-signed cert by default — keep "https+insecure". Use "http" ONLY if the hub runs with tls.enabled: false (a plain "http" rule against the TLS listener returns 502).
